about.note: North Conway is a village inside the Town of Conway, Carroll County, not a separate town, so this is the Town of Conway's record: its Board of Selectmen, Town Manager and annual Town Meeting. Conway uses the official ballot (SB2) form: a deliberative session in early March, then all articles voted by ballot at the April town election. North Conway's water, sewer and fire department are run by the separate North Conway Water Precinct. The town's Selectmen minutes sit in a Google Drive folder that could not be opened for this research, so meeting entries are built from the Conway Daily Sun, a meeting summary and town documents, and are marked as news reports. Plain-English summaries written by AI; items with needs_review=true are uncertain. On Agorri this is the Town of Conway inside the Mount Washington Valley page; North Conway, Conway Village, Center Conway, Kearsarge, Intervale and Redstone are all part of Conway.

issues.title: Police station addition and renovation
issues.status: Approved by voters April 14, 2026: $9.37 million bond passed 1,052-620, clearing the three-fifths needed
issues.summary: After two failed tries, voters approved borrowing to expand and renovate the Conway Police station on East Conway Road. The chief has asked for up to $3 million in federal money to offset the cost; work will be done in phases while the department keeps operating.
points: Article 3 asked for $9,372,828 (gross), to be borrowed; Selectmen recommended it 4-0-0 and the Budget Committee 11-1-0.
It passed 1,052-620; a three-fifths majority needed 1,023 yes votes.
In 2025 a $9,150,000 version (Article 18) got 1,116-845, short of three-fifths.

Chief Chris Mattei applied in February 2026 for FY2027 Congressionally Directed Spending (a federal earmark) with help from Sen. Shaheen's office; the Daily Sun reported up to $3 million could come from it. Award not confirmed.

issues.title: Rec Path Phase 2 through Whitaker Woods
issues.status: Petition Article 46 was on the April 14 ballot; supporters called the result disappointing (vote count not confirmed)
issues.summary: Supporters want a paved path from Cranmore through Whitaker Woods in North Conway and along the state rail corridor to Intervale, paid for only with grants and donations. Selectmen first backed the petition, then voted to oppose it; the Budget Committee also opposed it. The article was non-binding.
points: Estimated cost rose from $3.3 million to $5.6 million; a federal EDA grant was terminated because the timeline could not be met.
April 7: the Mt. Washington Valley Trails Association said it secured the last private easement along the power line corridor.
Selectmen voted 3-2 to support the petition, then after the March 4 deliberative session voted 2-1 to oppose it, with Seavey and Shepard abstaining.
Budget Committee opposed it 8-3-1. Town counsel said the article is non-binding.
After the vote, the Trails Association said the result was 'certainly disappointing' and its board would meet on next steps.

issues.title: North Conway Water Precinct: treating PFAS in landfill leachate
issues.status: Precinct voters approved an $8 million bond on March 25, 2026 (40-8)
issues.summary: The North Conway Water Precinct, a separate local government that runs North Conway's water, sewer and fire department, will design and build treatment for PFAS ('forever chemicals') in landfill leachate (liquid draining from the landfill) sent to its wastewater plant. Officials say the landfill's users should pay for it.
points: The $9.3 million proposal was cut to $8 million at the annual meeting by removing $1.3 million in plant buildings not tied to PFAS; it passed 40-8 by secret ballot.
A wastewater master planning article passed 41-3.
Superintendent Jason Gagnon said the precinct would not proceed without an agreement with the Mount Washington Valley Solid Waste District.
If the precinct paid it all, a 20-year note on about $6 million would cost about $367,000 a year, roughly 25 cents per $1,000 on the precinct tax rate (Feb 25 hearing estimate).
Officials said 35 to 70 percent of the PFAS at the plant comes from the landfill; $5 million or more in state aid may be available.
